title: Negotiating a one-time settlement with a bank from strength
p1:
Most people think a bank decides your settlement offer. That’s not always true.

The strongest negotiations often happen when the borrower understands their position better than the bank expects.
p2:
A common mistake is approaching a one-time settlement (OTS) with fear and immediately asking for a discount. Banks usually look at risk, recovery chances, time, and costs involved.

A surprising insight: a bank may prefer a reasonable settlement over a long recovery process that consumes years and resources.
p3:
Negotiating from strength means being prepared. Know your repayment history, your financial reality, the value of any security involved, and what makes a settlement beneficial for both sides.

The goal is not to avoid responsibility. It is to create a practical solution backed by facts, timing, and a clear proposal.
conclusion: Have you ever seen someone successfully negotiate a bank settlement? What factor do you think gives a borrower the strongest position?
